steps.title: Open Pair
steps.body: Our next strategy is called the Open Pair. When exactly two cells in a unit share the same two candidates, no other cells in that unit can share those candidates. Let's take a look!

steps.title: Spot the Pair
steps.body: In the top row, two cells share candidates 2 and 4 — an Open Pair.

steps.title: Why it Works
steps.body: Logically, one of these two cells must be 2 and the other must be 4. If we placed a 2 on the left cell, the other must be 4. If we placed a 2 on the right cell, the other must be 4. That means the 2 and 4 can't be anywhere else in the row!

steps.title: First Open Pair
steps.body: Here's where selecting multiple empty cells comes in! We are going to select the evidence of our strategy. First select one of the two cells with candidates 2 and 4, then select the other.

steps.title: Quick Single
steps.body: Before the next pair appears, press Hint then Apply to place this Naked Single.

steps.title: One More Single
steps.body: Press Hint then Apply once more to place the next Naked Single.

steps.title: Second Naked Pair
steps.body: Now in this row, two cells share candidates 5 and 7 — tap either cell of this Naked Pair.

steps.title: Great Work
steps.body: You identified two Naked Pairs. Use them to prune candidates and set up more singles and pairs as you continue.
